worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\frac{3}{4}x\le y\le 3-\frac{3}{4}x},
$$

 

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/1f332ebf554ac0e1b9e5099244aa50de0beef38c92efcba04e95e73abd21ecb6.png)

    

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}(2-x)|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}{(2-x)}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}[{\int }_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}[y]_{3x/4}^{3-3x/4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{3}(3-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{3x}{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(2-x)^{4}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{(2-x)^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(0-\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}) \\  & =\frac{48}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
